title: OTWONO ONM Content-Fetch Protocol
description: The messages two nodes exchange to move content over an authenticated ONM channel (ADR-0017). Every message travels inside one Noise transport frame after the Hello exchange, so every one is bounded: a requester asks for a range, a responder may answer with less, and the requester loops. There is exactly one error shape — absent, private, shared, damaged, and not-part-of-that-object all produce not_available, because any finer answer tells a stranger what this node holds. A chunk request names the object the chunk belongs to; a bare digest would be a probe against a content-addressed store.

digest.description: A BLAKE3 digest as 64 lowercase hex characters. Lowercase is required rather than normalised: these are compared byte for byte everywhere else, and two spellings would be two objects.

manifest_request.description: One window of an object's chunk list. Paginated because a 1 GiB object is roughly 16000 chunks at ADR-0016's 64 KiB average, and that list is far larger than any frame.

from_chunk.description: Index of the first chunk wanted.

max_chunks.description: How many entries the requester can receive in one reply. A responder builds the page in memory, so the ceiling is not negotiable.

chunk_request.description: One range of one chunk of one object. content_id is required and is not redundant: it is what stops the digest being a probe oracle.

max_bytes.description: How many bytes the requester can receive in one reply, capped at ADR-0016's MAX_CHUNK.

chunking.description: The chunking parameter set that produced this object (ADR-0016). A peer running different parameters can detect the mismatch, which is all it can do about it.

visibility.description: Only ever public or replicated. Nothing else may leave the node, so nothing else can appear here — and a receiver needs this to know whether it may re-serve what it caches.

length.description: Bounded by ADR-0016's MAX_CHUNK. A zero-length chunk is not something the chunker produces.

total_length.description: Length of the whole chunk, so a requester knows when it is done.

data.description: Base64 of the bytes at offset. May be shorter than asked for; never longer. Empty only when offset is already at total_length.

not_available.description: The only error. There is deliberately no reason field: absent, refused, damaged, and not-part-of-that-object must be indistinguishable.
